title: NBA2 v3 suggestions register — review before implementing
source_note: Proposals, not decisions. Each names what it would change, what it costs, and what would have to be true for it to be worth doing. Nothing here is implemented; the list exists so the owner can reject items cheaply.

suggestions.proposal: Ship the calibrated probability as the default published number, with the raw one beside it.
suggestions.rationale: The shrink beats a coin out of sample (0.6398 vs 0.6931) while the raw model loses to one (0.7082). Publishing the losing number as the headline, even with the fix visible, invites a reader to stop at the first figure.
suggestions.cost: Low. alpha is already fitted and disclosed; this is a default, not a calculation.
suggestions.would_need_to_be_true: alpha must be stable across seasons. See V3Q-05 — if it is not, the default would need re-fitting per window, which is a different risk.

suggestions.proposal: Replace the letter grade (A/B/C) with the disagreement number alone.
suggestions.rationale: The grade collapses a continuous signal into three buckets with hand-set thresholds (≤1.0 pts and |margin| ≥ 0.75σ), and a reader cannot see where a B line sits inside the B bucket.
suggestions.cost: Low, but it removes a scanning aid that the picks page relies on.
suggestions.would_need_to_be_true: Readable at a glance without the letter. A sorted table plus a colour ramp on the disagreement cell would probably do it.
suggestions.recommendation: pilot on the lines page only

suggestions.proposal: Add a second, independent estimate of sigma (e.g. from quarter-level scoring) and publish the gap.
suggestions.rationale: sigma is a single number fitted from whole-game residuals and drives both p_home and every total. If it is wrong, every probability is wrong in the same direction and no backtest on the same data can reveal it.
suggestions.cost: Medium — needs quarter data, which exists for only five games today.
suggestions.would_need_to_be_true: Quarter scores for a meaningful number of games. Currently 5 of 188, so this is blocked on the same capture gap as V3Q-03.
suggestions.recommendation: defer until quarter capture is routine

suggestions.proposal: Publish a per-club 'rating stability' series showing how much each club's rating moved date to date.
suggestions.rationale: A club whose rating swings 6 points a week is not measurable by a season-average model, and the site currently gives no way to see that.
suggestions.cost: Low — the walk-forward already computes every date's ratings; it discards them.
suggestions.would_need_to_be_true: Nothing. This is a display of an intermediate that already exists.

suggestions.proposal: Stop publishing the totals page's naive average column once the possession total is fixed.
suggestions.rationale: The brief asks for the comparison. If the possession total ever beats a constant, the naive figure becomes historical debt.
suggestions.would_need_to_be_true: The brief's requirement to show the comparison would have to be judged satisfied. Currently it is NOT — the possession total loses, so the comparison is still doing work.

suggestions.proposal: Make the ledger's verification a required check on every PR, not only on a schedule.
suggestions.rationale: A ledger that is verified nightly but not on the change that broke it lets a bad pick publish for a day.
suggestions.cost: One workflow step; already written in v3-verify.yml.
suggestions.would_need_to_be_true: Nothing. This is already the case for the v3 workflow and should stay that way.

suggestions.proposal: Add a 'what changed since yesterday' page generated by diffing consecutive payloads.
suggestions.rationale: Every number on this site moves. A reader returning the next day cannot tell whether a line moved because a game was played or because a capture changed.
suggestions.cost: Medium — needs the previous payload kept, which means committing data/v3/payload.json history.
suggestions.would_need_to_be_true: A retention decision on payload size (currently ~250 KB/day). Trimming to the summary fields would make it trivial.

suggestions.proposal: Retire v2 entirely once v3's blocked inputs are resolved.
suggestions.rationale: Two sites publishing overlapping projections is the confusion the surface split exists to prevent. Today they disagree about h (v2 uses a free-ish 2.0 constant; v3 pins 0.963).
suggestions.cost: High — v2 carries 60 flags, 25 questions and the audit history.
suggestions.would_need_to_be_true: v3 would need to carry forward every open v2 flag. Until then, v2 is the audit record and v3 is the model, and the dashboard link between them is honest about which is which.
